lint.unknownFunction: '{name}' is no function or variable this game or this code knows.

lint.unreachable: This code never runs: the code before it always leaves the block.

settings.title: Settings
settings.fontFamily: Font family (empty uses the theme font)

settings.backupsTip: Each backup is a full copy of the data file, so 100 backups of a 500 MB file take 50 GB on disk, and every save renames each backup once.
settings.askOnClose: Ask before closing with unsaved changes
settings.askRisky: Ask before risky actions and offer to do them anyway
settings.riskyNote: G3MStudio refuses some actions to protect your data. With the first option on, it explains the risk and lets you do the action anyway. With the second option on, it does the action at once with no warning. Undo still works until you save. Use the second option only if you know what can go wrong.
settings.roomGridOverride: Use one grid for every room
settings.rememberWindow: Open the window where it was closed
settings.startupRestore: Reopen the last file, tabs and layout
settings.lostSearch: Look for a lost data file by its hash in nearby folders and the folders of recent files

settings.mismatchPolicy: When a data file differs from the one remembered
settings.mismatchKeep: Open it and keep the saved layout
settings.mismatchFresh: Open it with a fresh layout
settings.lostForget: Remove the old entry from Recent when a replacement file is chosen
settings.warnTempRun: Warn that a run is a temporary copy
settings.projectsNote: These are the defaults for new projects; changing them also changes the open project.
settings.advancedNote: Any token of the theme can be set in settings.json under "overrides", for example "Bg.Overlay": "#E61B1B1B" or "Radius.Window": "10". The file reloads as soon as you save it.
settings.crashNote: Only releases that carry a key send anything. A report has the error text and its stack, the app, system and data file format facts, and the commands and tab in use. Folder and file names, resource names, e-mail and IP addresses, and your user and computer name are replaced before sending, and the game's code, strings and files are never sent.
settings.usageStats: Share anonymous usage statistics (sessions, speed, which features are used)
settings.installIdNote: A random number made on this PC. It tells one install from another in the reports and is made from nothing about you or this machine. Reset gives this install a new one.
settings.restoreTip: Resets the settings of the selected section.
settings.assocStop: Stop opening data files with G3MStudio

settings.linksFailed: The links could not be registered

settings.showNullEntries: Show null entries in the resource tree
settings.hoverPreviews: Show previews and IDs on hover
settings.profilesNote: The run profile you pick is remembered for each data file.
settings.shortcutClash: {shortcut} is set for {user} and is also the default of {other}. {user} runs on that key.

privacy.title: What is sent
privacy.intro: Both switches are on by default, and nothing is sent before the welcome window is closed. Crash reports must be on for anything to be sent. Both can be changed in Settings > Privacy.
privacy.crash: The error text and its stack, the versions of the app and G3MLib, the system (Windows version, processor type, memory size class), the commands and the kind of tab in use, a few settings (language, theme, scale) and the format facts of the data file (game version, size class). Sessions that start, end or crash.
privacy.usage: How long a session lasts, how fast opening, saving and tabs are, how many resources a file has (as a size class), which commands and editors are used and how often (one summary per session), the update check result, and notes about start-up and hangs.
privacy.never: Folder, file, user and computer names. Names of resources, objects, sprites and rooms. The game's code, texts, pictures and sounds. Anything you type, except feedback you choose to send. E-mail and IP addresses, keys. The only identifier is a random install ID that you can reset.
privacy.off: With crash reports off, nothing is sent. With only usage statistics off, only errors and crash sessions are sent.

feedback.title: Send Feedback
feedback.contact: Contact (optional, sent only if you fill it in)
feedback.diagnostics: Include diagnostics (versions, system facts, the random install ID and the recent steps)
feedback.sends: Sent: your message with paths, e-mail and IP addresses removed, the contact if you typed one, and the diagnostics if the box is checked. Never sent: files, screenshots, or names of your folders, resources and computer.
feedback.off: Reporting is off. Turn on crash reports in Settings > Privacy to send feedback, or use Help > Report a Problem.
feedback.failed: The feedback could not be sent.

onboarding.title: Welcome to G3MStudio
onboarding.heading: Welcome to G3MStudio
onboarding.body: G3MStudio edits GameMaker games: sprites, rooms, code, sounds and more. It also builds mods and patches. Every choice can be changed later.
onboarding.usage: Share anonymous usage statistics (sessions, speed, which features are used)
onboarding.associate: Open GameMaker data files (.win, .unx, ...) with G3MStudio
onboarding.later: You can change the language later in Settings > Appearance, and open this window again from Help > Getting Started.

startup.askBody: Open {name}, where you stopped last time?

lostFile.title: Data file not found
lostFile.missing: G3MStudio cannot find {name} at {path}. It may have been moved, renamed or deleted. Choose the file again, and G3MStudio keeps its layout and sizes when the content is the same.
lostFile.unreadable: {name} at {path} cannot be read: {reason}. Another program may be using it, or you may not have permission.
lostFile.changed: {name} is not the same as when G3MStudio last saw it. It was changed outside G3MStudio, is another version of the game, or is another file. The layout and sizes G3MStudio kept belong to the earlier content.
lostFile.pick: Files that may be the one:
lostFile.none: No file with the same content was found nearby.
lostFile.keep: Keep the saved layout and sizes for this file
lostFile.found: Found {name} at {path}. It has the same content, so its layout and sizes are kept.
lostFile.refused: {name} is not the file G3MStudio remembered, and your settings say not to open it. Settings > Files changes this.

links.downloadAsk: Download the file at {address} from {host}? It is saved to a temporary folder and only opened if it is a game data file.
links.needsGame: Open a game data file first, then start a new mod from its changes.

explorer.title: Find anything
explorer.text: Every resource of the game is here, grouped by type. Press Ctrl+P to jump to any resource by name.

tabs.title: Open many things
tabs.text: A single click previews a resource in an italic tab. Edit it or double-click to keep it.

inspector.title: See what is selected
inspector.text: The Inspector shows the type and name of the selected resource, how many places use it, and the layers of the room in front.

palette.title: Every command is searchable
palette.text: Press Ctrl+Shift+P to search every command. The menus show the shortcuts.

problems.title: See what went wrong
problems.text: Warnings and errors from loading, saving and compiling collect here. Double-click one to jump to it.

save.title: Safe saving, quick testing
save.text: Save writes a new file and keeps a backup. Run Game starts the game with your changes without touching the original.

scripts.sourceFolder: Choose from the Scripts folder next to the program
scripts.commandLabel: C# code to run on the current data file
scripts.pickFile: The script asks for a file
scripts.pickFolder: The script asks for a folder
scripts.pickSave: The script asks where to save
scripts.title: Run script
scripts.confirm:
Run {name}?

A script can change anything in the data file and can read and write any file on this computer. The change cannot be undone; Revert to Saved is the way back. Only run scripts you trust.

This runs UndertaleModTool-style .csx scripts, but only part of that tool's functions exist here: Data, FilePath, ScriptPath, ScriptMessage, ScriptWarning, ScriptError and ScriptQuestion (answered yes). Scripts that need dialogs, the decompiler helpers or the UI stop with a compile error that names the missing function.

inspector.none: Select a resource in the Explorer.

image.keepRatioTip: Changing one side changes the other, so the proportions stay.
image.unitTip: Pixel sizes start at the current size of the picture. The unit and the percents are remembered for the next dialog.
image.scaleBoxTip: On: the collision box, its margins and the origin of the sprite are scaled with the picture. Off: they keep their pixel values, and a mask is read again from the new pixels only where it has to be.
image.scaleBoxOff: This choice applies only to Resize image. Resize canvas always moves the box and the origin with the pixels.
image.fillOff: The fill applies only to Resize canvas. Resize image stretches the picture over the whole canvas.
image.methodOff: The method applies only to Resize image. Resize canvas keeps the pixels as they are.
image.anchorOff: The anchor applies only to Resize canvas. Resize image stretches the whole picture.
image.anchorTip: Where the picture sits on the new canvas. A smaller canvas cuts the other sides.
image.fillTip: The colour of the area a larger canvas adds.
image.methodTip: Nearest keeps hard pixel edges. Bilinear blends neighbouring pixels.
image.modeTip: Resize image stretches the picture and the canvas together. Resize canvas changes only the canvas: the picture keeps its pixels.
image.limitFont: Font sheet: glyph rectangles follow a canvas change; scaling, rotating or skewing the whole sheet is refused
image.dragHint: Drag an edge or corner of the picture to change the canvas size. Shift keeps the aspect, Ctrl stretches the picture too, Esc cancels.
image.dragHintAll: Drag an edge or corner of the picture to change the canvas size. Shift keeps the aspect, Ctrl stretches the picture too, {key} applies it to all frames, Esc cancels.
image.limitPage: Texture page of {w}x{h}; the size cannot change
image.limitMask: Collision mask of {w}x{h}, 1 bit: white is solid, the size is fixed
image.limitIncluded: Loose file: Apply writes it to the game folder at once (JPEG has no transparency, a GIF keeps its first frame)
image.limitGlyph: Glyph of {w}x{h} on the font sheet; the size is fixed and Apply writes the sheet
image.conflictAsk: {name} changed elsewhere after you started editing it. Applying replaces those changes with your edits. Apply anyway, or discard your edits?
image.conflictKept: Your edits are kept and not applied. The sprite changed elsewhere.
image.applyFirstBlocked: The sprite changed elsewhere, so your edits cannot be applied first. Apply or discard them, then try again.
image.locked: This layer is locked. Unlock it to change its pixels.
image.layerHidden: This layer is hidden. Show it to draw on it.
image.stale: The picture changed elsewhere while you drew, so this edit was not applied and the picture was read again.
image.discardBlocked: Other edits came in after yours, so Discard cannot take back only yours. Use Undo.
image.savedNew: Saved the picture as the new sprite {name}.
image.saveAllAsNewTip: Make one new sprite with every frame. The original stays as it is.
image.closeAsk: {name} has edits that are not applied. Apply them, or discard them?
image.changedElsewhere: The picture of {name} changed elsewhere after you opened it. Applying replaces that change with your picture. Apply anyway?
image.applyTip: Keep the edits made since the editor opened or since the last Apply.
image.discardTip: Drop the edits made since the editor opened or since the last Apply.
image.saveAsNewTip: Make a new sprite from this frame. The original stays as it is.
image.notApplied: The edits to {name} were not applied: {reason}
image.noPicture: This tab has no picture to edit.
image.noFrames: This sprite has no frames to edit.

hint.Pencil: Click to paint. Ctrl picks a colour. Right button paints the second colour.
hint.Eraser: Click or drag to erase to transparent.
hint.Replace: Click a pixel: every pixel of that colour becomes the primary colour.
hint.Remove: Click a pixel: every pixel of that colour becomes transparent.
hint.Fill: Click to fill the area. Tolerance and Contiguous are in the options bar.
hint.Rectangle: Drag. Alt draws from the centre, Shift keeps it square.
hint.Ellipse: Drag. Alt draws from the centre, Shift keeps it a circle.
hint.Polygon: Click the corners. Enter or a double click closes it, Escape cancels.
hint.Curve: Click three or four control points. Enter or a double click draws the curve.
hint.Picker: Click to pick the primary colour, right click for the secondary.
hint.Select: Drag a rectangle. Escape clears the selection.
hint.Lasso: Drag around the pixels to select.
hint.Wand: Click to select similar pixels. Tolerance and Contiguous are in the options bar.
hint.Move: Drag to move the selection (or the whole picture). Arrow keys nudge by 1, Shift by 8.
hint.Hand: Drag to move the view; the picture does not change. Space or the middle button moves the view with any tool, Ctrl+wheel zooms and the wheel scrolls.
hint.Text: Type the text in the options bar, then click to place it in the primary colour.

image.allFramesToggleTip: Apply a handle resize to every frame of the sprite. Off: only the selected frame changes.

roomOrder.title: Room Order
roomOrder.hint: The first room is where the game starts. Rooms that are not listed cannot be reached with room_goto_next.

audio.title: Edit audio of {sound}
audio.notApplied: The sound was not changed. Apply again, or cancel.
audio.loopTip: Play the sound again from the start when it ends.
audio.loopRegionTip: Play again from the start when the end is reached: the region when one is set, otherwise the whole sound.
audio.playRegionTip: Play only the region. With Loop on, the region repeats.
audio.regionFieldTip: Start or end of the region, in seconds. A change applies at once, also while the sound plays.
audio.regionHint: Drag on the waveform to select a region. Click to move the playback position. Drag the edges of the region to adjust it, or drag its middle to move it. Shift+click moves the nearest edge, and the arrow keys move the edge you used last (with Shift in larger steps). Ctrl+drag inside the region selects a new one. Double-click the waveform or use Clear region to remove it, and press Esc to cancel a selection. Changes apply while the sound plays. Start and end can also be typed in the fields.
audio.clearRegionTip: Remove the region, so the whole sound plays again.
audio.saveRegionHint: Only the region is saved when one is set, otherwise the whole sound.
audio.noDevice: No audio output device was found, so the sound cannot play here.
audio.noLibrary: The OpenAL library could not be loaded, so sound plays through the system player. Put {file} in the folder next to the program.
audio.notWav: Only a sound stored in the file as WAV, OGG or MP3 can be edited here. Select one, or use Replace Audio.
audio.zoomInTip: Zoom in on the time axis. Ctrl+wheel zooms at the pointer, the + key zooms at the cursor.
audio.zoomOutTip: Zoom out on the time axis. Ctrl+wheel zooms at the pointer, the - key zooms at the cursor.
audio.fitTip: Show the whole sound. While zoomed in, the wheel scrolls the waveform.
audio.zoomAtMax: Already zoomed in as far as it goes.
audio.zoomAtAll: The whole sound is already shown.
audio.visualizerTip: Show a level meter (peak and RMS, left and right) and a spectrum while the sound plays. Hidden, it does no work.

synth.title: Generate sound
synth.randomTip: Fill all values with a random sound. The values are shown, so you can keep the sound or change it.
synth.seedTip: The same seed and values always give the same sound. The seed sets the noise.
synth.dutyTip: The duty only changes the square wave; it is off for the other shapes.
synth.name: Name of the new sound
synth.noName: Enter a name for the new sound.
synth.replaceNone: Replace audio of the selected sound
synth.replaceTip: Put this sound into the selected sound. One undo step brings the old audio back.
synth.editorTip: Make a sound with the generator to replace the audio of this sound. This editor closes once the audio is replaced.

record.title: Record sound
record.refreshTip: Look for microphones again, for example after you plug one in.
record.locked: This cannot be changed while a recording is in progress.
record.gainTip: Makes the recording louder or quieter while it is recorded. Above 100 percent a loud sound can clip.
record.gainDone: The gain applies while recording. Record again to use another gain.
record.clipping: Clipping: the sound reached the loudest possible level and is distorted. Lower the input gain or move away from the microphone, then record again.
record.countdownTip: Wait three seconds after you press Record, so you have time to get ready.
record.startBusy: A recording is already in progress. Press Stop to finish it.
record.pauseTip: Pause works while a recording is running.
record.stopTip: Stop works while a recording is running or about to start.
record.stateIdle: Ready. Nothing is recorded until you press Record.
record.stateDone: Recording finished. Listen to it, drag on the waveform to choose the part to keep, then make a sound of it.
record.info: Keeps {seconds} of {total} seconds, 44100 Hz, mono, 16 bit WAV
record.discard: The recording is not in a sound yet. If you go on, it is lost.
record.empty: Nothing was recorded. Check that the microphone works and press Record again.
record.capReached: The recording reached the longest take that can be stored and stopped. What was recorded is kept.
record.memoryStop: The recording stopped because memory is running low. What was recorded is kept.
record.failLibrary: The OpenAL library could not be loaded, so the microphone cannot be used. Put {file} in the folder next to the program.
record.failNoDevice: No microphone was found. Connect one and press Refresh.
record.failBusy: The microphone could not be opened. Another program may be using it. Stop that program and try again.
record.failDenied: The system does not allow this program to use the microphone. Allow it in the privacy options of your system, then press Refresh.
record.failLost: The microphone stopped working. The recording up to that moment is kept.
record.editorTip: Record your voice to replace the audio of this sound. This editor closes once the audio is replaced.

dock.StudioToolPinTip: Unpin: auto-hide this panel to the side

debug.assembler: Assembler, marks at stores, jumps and returns

hex.size: {bytes} bytes on disk. This is the saved file, not unsaved edits. Patches change the file only when you write them.

copyTo.mode: When the name exists in the target:
copyTo.nothing: Nothing to copy with these settings.
copyTo.pickTarget: Pick the data file to copy into
copyTo.noSelection: Select the resources to copy in the Explorer first.
copyTo.sameFile: That is the file you copy from. Use Duplicate to copy inside one data file.
copyTo.done: {count} {count:resource|resources} copied to {target}. One Undo takes {count:it|them all} out.
copyTo.saveAsk: {target} was opened only for this copy. Save it now? If you say no, the copy is dropped.
copyTo.cancelled: The copy was cancelled; nothing changed.
copyTo.keepOrganizeAsk: Put the copied resources in the same folders, collections and tags in {target}?
copyTo.keptOrganize: Folders, collections and tags kept in {target}.

included.empty: There are no included files next to this data file.

risky.includedPictureTitle: Write the picture into the game folder?
risky.includedTextTitle: Write the text into the game folder?
risky.includedText:
{reason}

The data file does not hold this change.
risky.includedAudioTitle: Write the audio into the game folder?
risky.includedAudio:
{reason}

The data file does not hold this change.
risky.includedPicture:
{reason}

The data file does not hold this change.
risky.includedRename:
{reason}

The game looks the file up by its name, so it may not find it after the rename. This cannot be undone.
risky.includedDelete:
{reason}

The game may fail where it loads this file. The file is moved to the G3MStudio trash folder.
risky.audioSizeTitle: Put in a very large audio file anyway?
risky.audioSize:
{reason}

A very large sound uses a lot of memory when the data file is opened and saved, and the game can fail to load it. Undo takes it out again until you save.
risky.audioKindTitle: Put in audio of another kind anyway?
risky.audioKind:
{reason}

The sound keeps its old type and flags, so the game may not play audio of another kind. Undo brings the old audio back until you save.
risky.pageSizeTitle: Replace the page with a picture of another size?
risky.pageSize:
{reason}

Every sprite frame, glyph and tile on this page points at a rectangle on it. With another size they can show the wrong part or nothing. Undo brings the old picture back until you save.
risky.tileGridTitle: Change the size or corner of the tile set picture {name}?
risky.tileGrid:
{reason}

Rooms place tiles by their number on this grid. When the picture shrinks or its top left moves, tiles show the wrong part or nothing. Grow the canvas to the right or down to keep every tile. Undo brings the old picture back until you save.
risky.lastFrame:
{reason}

A sprite without frames draws nothing, and the game can fail where it uses {name}. Undo puts the frame back until you save.
risky.lastPoint:
{reason}

An empty path can make the game fail where it follows {name}. Undo puts the point back until you save.
risky.importType:
{reason}

If you go on, G3MStudio reads the file as text and makes a script from it. A file that is not GML will not compile as it is. Undo removes the script until you save.
risky.copySizeTitle: Copy a very large package anyway?
risky.copySize:
{reason}

The whole package is held in memory and in the journal, so G3MStudio can run out of memory or become slow. Undo removes the copy until you save.
risky.collisionTitle: Delete {name} and the events that aim at it?
risky.collision:
{reason}

If you go on, those collision events and their code are removed from the other objects. Undo brings them back until you save.
risky.roomPngTitle: Save a reduced picture of the room?
risky.roomPng:
{reason}

If you go on, the picture is made smaller so that its longer side is 16384 pixels. It is not pixel for pixel.
risky.unsavedBulk: You have unsaved changes. This action cannot be undone, so the undo history is cleared. The unsaved changes stay in the file in memory but can no longer be undone, and crash recovery starts again from here. Save first if you are unsure.
risky.unsavedExport: You have unsaved changes. The mod or patch is made from the saved file on disk, so they are not in it. Save first to include them.
risky.hexPatch:
{reason}

A wrong byte can make the file unreadable or the game fail. This cannot be undone: the file is changed on disk and loaded again. Keep a copy first.
risky.chunkImport:
{reason}

If the new bytes have another length, every chunk after it moves and the offsets stored inside the file are not adjusted, so the file may not load. This cannot be undone: keep a copy first.

modBase.cleared: The mod base cache is empty.
modBase.lost: The saved copy of the original is missing or damaged. Choose the original file.
modBase.mismatch: That file does not match the saved original (the hash differs). Nothing was exported.

chunks.pick: Chunk of the data file on disk
chunks.pickIn: File with the new chunk bytes
chunks.sameFile: The output must be a different file from the data file and its backup.
chunks.imported: Chunk {name} replaced from {file}. The file is loaded again.
chunks.none: The file on disk has no chunks (it is not a FORM file).
chunks.unsavedReload: You have unsaved changes. The file is loaded again after this write, so they are dropped. Save first if you are unsure.
chunks.reason: This writes raw bytes into the data file on disk.
chunks.otherFile: The data file in use is no longer the one this action started with. Nothing was written.
chunks.reloadFailed: The data file could not be opened again after the write. The backup {file} holds the file from before the write.
